title: Introduction to sets
competency: Explain what is meant by a set and by an element.

keywords.def: We can clearly decide if an object belongs or not.
One of the objects in a set. Also called a member.
A set with no element. Written { } or ∅.

en.text: A set is a collection of well-defined objects. Well-defined means we can clearly decide if an object belongs. The vowels a, e, i, o, u form a set. The tall students in a class do not, because tall is not clear.

screens.title: Tall students
screens.ask: Can we write "all the tall students in your class" as a set?
opts: Yes, everyone agrees who is tall
Only if the class is small
screens.after:
People disagree about who is tall.
Is 1.55 m tall? Is 1.60 m? There is no clear rule.
So "the tall students" is not a set.
A set needs a clear yes-or-no rule.

screens.title: 1.1 Introduction to sets
paras: In mathematics, a set describes a collection of objects.
Each object must be well-defined. We must be able to decide if it belongs or not.

screens.title: Definition 1.1
paras: Set is a collection of well-defined objects.
The objects in a set are called members or elements.
We list the elements between braces { }, separated by commas.
We name sets with capital letters, like A = {a, e, i, o, u}.
screens.note: Each element is listed once. The order does not matter.

screens.title: Set or not a set?
items: A set: {0, 1, 2, 3}. The rule is clear.
Five most talented writers of Ethiopia
Not a set. No rule says who is "most talented".
A set: {a, e, i, o, u}.

screens.title: The yes-or-no test
steps: January? Yes. February? No. March? No.
Every month gets a clear yes or no.
So it is well-defined: {January, June, July} is a set.
Now try: the tall students in your class.
Is Abebe tall? Some say yes, some say no.
No clear answer, so it is not a set.

screens.title: Key words
defs: We can clearly decide if an object belongs or not.

screens.text: Well-defined: which collection is a set?
opts: The intelligent students in your class
The months of the year that start with "J"
The best footballers in Addis Ababa
screens.ans: The months of the year that start with "J"
screens.why:
A set needs a clear yes-or-no rule.
"Intelligent" is an opinion. People disagree.
"Best footballers" is also an opinion.
For each month we can say yes or no: January, June, July.
So the months that start with "J" form a set.
screens.clue: Which one has a clear yes/no rule?

screens.title: Sort the collections: set or not a set?
screens.why:
Ask one question: is there a clear rule?
Whole numbers less than 4, vowels and regions can be listed.
"Beautiful", "talented" and "tall" are opinions.
Opinions are not well-defined, so those are not sets.
screens.clue: Ask: could two people disagree about it?

screens.ask: Complete the set of vowels: A = {a, e, ___, o, u}.
screens.why:
The English vowels are a, e, i, o, u.
The set shows a, e, o and u.
The missing vowel is i.
screens.clue: Which vowel comes between e and o?

screens.text: Is it well-defined? Hana says: "The set of large numbers is a set." Is she right?
opts: Yes, but only for whole numbers
screens.why:
Is 100 large? Is 1,000? People disagree.
So "large" gives no clear rule.
No: it is not well-defined, so it is not a set.
A fix: "numbers greater than 100" is a set.
"Only whole numbers" does not help; "large" is still unclear.
screens.clue: Could two people disagree about which numbers are large?

en.text: The objects in a set are its elements. We write a ∈ A when a is an element of A. We write a ∉ A when it is not. For N = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, 6 ∈ N and 3 ∉ N.

screens.title: Is it inside?
screens.after:
Look between the braces: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
3 is not listed.
So 3 is not an element of N.

screens.title: Elements
paras: If a is a member of set A, we write a ∈ A. Read: a is an element of A.
If a is not a member of A, we write a ∉ A. Read: a is not an element of A.

screens.title: True or false?
steps: a. 6 ∈ N is true: 6 is in N.
b. 12 ∉ N is true: 12 is not in N.
c. 3 ∈ N is false: 3 is not in N.
d. 2 ∉ N is false: 2 is in N.

screens.title: Key words
defs: One of the objects in a set. Also called a member.

screens.why:
N = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}.
Look for 8 between the braces.
8 is listed, so 8 ∈ N.
The statement is true.

screens.text: Element or not? True or false: 0 ∈ {0.5, 1.2, 4, 10}
screens.why:
The elements are 0.5, 1.2, 4 and 10.
0.5 starts with 0, but it is not the number 0.
0 itself is not listed.
So 0 ∉ the set. The statement is false.

screens.text: Continue the pattern. True or false: 10 ∈ {0, 2, 4, …}
screens.why:
The dots mean the pattern goes on.
Add 2 each time: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, …
10 is reached.
So 10 ∈ the set. True.
screens.clue: Continue the pattern: add 2 each time.

screens.text: Not an element: A = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Tap every number that is ∉ A.
screens.why:
∉ means "is not an element of".
A holds 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
1, 5 and 9 are in A, so they are ∈ A.
2, 6 and 10 are not listed.
So 2 ∉ A, 6 ∉ A and 10 ∉ A.

screens.title: N = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}: sort each number, ∈ N or ∉ N?
items: 5 is odd; N lists only even numbers.
screens.why:
N lists 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 only.
Listed: 4 and 10, so 4 ∈ N and 10 ∈ N.
Not listed: 0, 5 and 12.
So 0 ∉ N, 5 ∉ N and 12 ∉ N.
screens.clue: Look between the braces for each number.

screens.text: Continue the pattern. True or false: 8 ∉ {1, 3, 5, …}
screens.why:
The pattern adds 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, …
These are the odd numbers.
It jumps from 7 to 9. It never reaches 8.
8 is even, so 8 is not an element.
"8 ∉" says exactly that. True.
screens.clue: Continue the pattern. Is 8 ever reached?

ideas.name: Counting elements and the empty set

en.text: A repeated element counts once, so {1, 2, 4, 1} has 3 elements. A set with no element is the empty set, written { } or ∅. The set of cats that can fly is empty.

screens.title: A hundred years old
screens.ask: List all students in your class who are 100 years old. How many are there?
screens.after:
Nobody in a Grade 7 class is 100 years old.
So the list has no names at all.
A set with no element is the empty set.

screens.title: How many elements?
paras: Repeating an element does not add a new element.
There is no whole number less than 0. So that set has no element.
screens.note: Natural numbers start at 1. Whole numbers start at 0.

screens.title: Note
paras: A set with no element is called the empty set.
We use { } or ∅ for the empty set.

screens.title: Empty or not? Tap each set.
Key words
defs: A set with no element. Written { } or ∅.

screens.text: Empty set: which set has no element?
opts: The set of rivers in Ethiopia
The set of whole numbers between 4 and 5
The set of whole numbers less than 4
screens.ans: The set of whole numbers between 4 and 5
screens.why:
Count the whole numbers between 4 and 5.
After 4 the next whole number is 5.
Nothing lies between them, so the set is empty.
Rivers of Ethiopia: Abay, Baro, … not empty.
Whole numbers less than 4: 0, 1, 2, 3. Not empty.
screens.clue: Is there a whole number between 4 and 5?

screens.ask: Count the elements: A = {2, 2, 2, 2} has ___ element(s).
screens.why:
A repeated element counts only once.
The only different number is 2.
So A = {2}.
A has 1 element.
screens.clue: How many different numbers are listed?

screens.ask: Count the elements: D = the set of whole numbers less than 6. D has ___ elements.
screens.why:
Whole numbers start at 0.
Those less than 6: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Count them: 6 numbers.
D has 6 elements. (Not 5: do not forget 0.)

screens.title: Sort: empty set or not?
screens.why:
A set is empty if you cannot name one element.
Natural numbers start at 1, so none is less than 1: empty.
No Grade 7 student is 30: empty.
Trees in Addis Ababa and months with "J" have elements: not empty.
screens.clue: Can you name even one element?

screens.text: Spot the non-empty set: which of these is NOT the empty set?
screens.why:
{ } and ∅ are two ways to write the empty set.
No natural number lies between 20 and 21: empty.
{0} has one element: the number 0.
So {0} is not empty. It looks like "nothing", but 0 is an element.
screens.clue: Count the elements inside the braces.

screens.title: Natural and whole numbers
steps: Natural numbers are the counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, …
Whole numbers are the natural numbers and 0: 0, 1, 2, 3, …
So 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.

screens.text: Whole numbers: how many whole numbers are less than 3?
screens.why:
Whole numbers start at 0.
Those less than 3: 0, 1, 2.
That is 3 numbers.

items.why:
The elements are 0.5, 1.2, 4 and 10.
0.5 is not the same as 0.
0 is not listed, so 0 ∉ the set.
False.

The pattern adds 2 each time.
0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, …
10 is in the pattern.
True.

∉ says "1 is not an element".
But 1 is the first element listed.
So 1 ∈ the set.
The statement is false.

The pattern is 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, …: odd numbers.
8 is even, so it never appears.
So 8 ∉ the set.
True.

items.text: Is "the collection of intelligent students in your class" a set?
items.why:
A set needs a clear rule.
Who is "intelligent"? People disagree.
So the collection is not well-defined.
It is not a set.

items.text: Is "the months of the year which start with letter J" a set?
items.why:
Check each month: does it start with J?
January, June and July do. The rest do not.
The rule is clear: {January, June, July}.
So it is a set.

items.text: Is "the natural numbers between 20 and 21" a set?
items.why:
The rule is clear: a natural number between 20 and 21.
After 20 the next natural number is 21.
No number fits the rule.
A clear rule with no members is the empty set.
So it is a set: the empty set.
items.clue: A clear rule with no members still gives a set.

items.ask: Count the elements: C = { } has ___ elements.
items.why:
Look between the braces.
Nothing is there.
{ } is the empty set.
C has 0 elements.

items.ask: Count the elements: B = {a, b} has ___ elements.
items.why:
The elements are a and b.
They are different letters.
B has 2 elements.

items.text: Empty or not? M = the set of students in your class whose age is 30 years.
items.why:
Grade 7 students are about 12 to 14 years old.
Nobody in the class is 30.
So M has no element.
M is the empty set.

test.text: Well-defined: which collection is a set?
opts: The kind people in your town
test.why:
A set needs a clear yes-or-no rule.
"Kind" and "best" are opinions.
Whole numbers less than 5 are clear: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
So the whole numbers less than 5 form a set.

test.text: A = {a, e, i, o, u}. True or false: b ∈ A.
test.why:
A = {a, e, i, o, u}, the vowels.
b is not a vowel.
b is not listed in A, so b ∉ A.
The statement is false.

Repeated elements count only once.
The different elements are 3 and 7.
So the set is {3, 7}.
It has 2 elements.

test.text: Empty set: which set has no element?
test.why:
Whole numbers start at 0.
No whole number is less than 0: this set is empty.
{0} has one element, the number 0.
Even numbers less than 3 are 0 and 2: not empty.

test.ask: Count the elements: E = the set of even natural numbers less than 10. E has ___ elements.
test.why:
Natural numbers start at 1, so 0 is not included.
Even ones less than 10: 2, 4, 6, 8.
Count them: 4.
E = {2, 4, 6, 8} has 4 elements.
